subject: Proposed tri-region supply rebalance & deal-priority matrix
messages:
From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Fri, 10 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Proposed tri-region supply rebalance & deal-priority matrix

Karthik / Marissa —

Attached is my first pass at rebalance numbers for Q3 to align dedicated pools with our highest-probability deals. Key points up front:

- Seastone (DEAL-8342) needs strong APAC presence for their launch but will accept an initial US fallback for 6 weeks if we commit burst capacity.
- CloudZone expansion (DEAL-8390) pushes steady EU demand starting mid-July; EU availability looks tight in the current procurement plan.
- We have limited APAC spare nodes in our hosted region but could re-route some Dedicated burst from US if we stagger rollouts.

Please review the attached tri_region_rebalance_v1.xlsx — it includes per-deal token/day projections, estimated GPU-hours, and a recommended transfer plan (US -> APAC, EU retention). I think we should approve the transfer plan and start procurement conversations for two additional APAC A100-equivalent instances to cover peak weeks.

Ask: can you both review today and call out any additional constraints (legal/region pricing/partner commitments) before EOD so I can present this to Procurement on Monday?

Thanks,
Priya
Priya Natarajan
Sr. Sales Operations Manager | Redwood Inference
priya.natarajan@redwood.com
(415) 555-0192

Attachments:
- tri_region_rebalance_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Apr 2027 12:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed tri-region supply rebalance & deal-priority matrix

Priya —

Reviewed the sheet quickly. A few thoughts:

- The APAC buffer in your model is 18% of forecasted token-hours; recommend bumping to 25% for two reasons: partner onboarding often increases inference churn in week 1 and our queueing model assumes conservative batching.
- For EU, I don't think we can commit the 6x steady nodes you're showing unless we lock a spot with CloudZone; their next procurement window has a 6-week lead time. We should consider a temporary cross-region routing rule (EU requests routed to US-dedicated pool with geo-tagged priority) for non-latency-critical customers.
- If Procurement can start a soft-commit for two APAC nodes this week (non-binding), we should be able to cover Seastone's launch with the US fallback + caching.

I'll mark comments directly on tri_region_rebalance_v1.xlsx and follow up.

-k
Karthik Iyer
Director, Deal Engineering | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 11 Apr 2027 08:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed tri-region supply rebalance & deal-priority matrix

All —

Two operational constraints to call out from Infrastructure:

1) EU capacity is constrained specifically on the GPU vendor side (slot availability in the region) — see attached capacity_constraints_EU.pdf from Sourcing. If we reassign EU-bound nodes to APAC, it will create a backlog for existing EU renewals. We need a prioritized deal list to minimize customer impact.

2) APAC provisioning lead time is 3-4 weeks if we go through our usual marketplace vendors; if we want sub-2-week lead times we need to use burst partners at 1.4x unit cost.

Proposal:
- Prioritize DEAL-8342 (Seastone) and DEAL-8390 (CloudZone) as top-2.
- Approve one APAC soft-commit (procurement to open paperwork) + a 2-week US fallback plan for Seastone with latency SLA <= 180ms.
- Maintain at least 10% spare capacity in EU to protect renewals.

I'll coordinate with Sourcing to get a vendor quote matrix Monday and can join the procurement call.

Marissa Cole
Head of Dedicated Operations | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Attachments:
- capacity_constraints_EU.pdf (report)
From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 10:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed tri-region supply rebalance & deal-priority matrix

Thanks both — summary below and next steps so we have a single action list for Procurement/Legal/CS:

Decision summary:
- Approve Seastone (DEAL-8342) as priority #1 for APAC allocation; fund a 2-week US fallback plan during first-month ramp.
- Approve CloudZone (DEAL-8390) as priority #2 for EU steady capacity; start vendor outreach for EU slots but keep 10% spare capacity for renewals.
- Procurement to open non-binding soft-commit for 1 APAC node (A100-equivalent) and an option for a second APAC node if week-over-week utilization exceeds 70%.

Action items (owners):
- Procurement (Karthik): open vendor soft-commit and gather 3 quotes (due Thu 15 Apr). HubSpot link to deals included below.
- Sourcing/Infra (Marissa): confirm EU lead-time and list of impacted renewals; prepare routing fallback plan for US -> APAC.
- Priya: finalize Deal Priority Matrix and email Seastone ops to confirm their latency acceptance and DocuSign for committed capacity.

I attached the initial deal_priority_matrix.csv that maps token-hour estimates to pool assignments. If we agree, I will email Seastone and loop in Procurement to get paperwork started.

Thanks — please reply with a short "approve" and I will proceed.

Priya

Attachments:
- deal_priority_matrix.csv (CSV)
Related links:
- https://hubspot.redwood/deals/DEAL-8342
From: Lina Gomez <lina@seastone.ai>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2027 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed tri-region supply rebalance & deal-priority matrix

Hi Priya / team —

Thanks for the clear plan and for prioritizing Seastone. Confirming Seastone can accept the initial US fallback for the first two weeks of our launch under two conditions:

1) Measured 95th percentile latency to our primary APAC user population must be <= 180ms when served from the US fallback pool (we will provide a synthetic test profile).
2) We need a signed capacity commitment (DocuSign) that covers the committed nodes for the first 90 days; please share the DocuSign routing link and the SLA appendix language (latency targets and credits).

We can sign quickly if Procurement can surface the DocuSign this week. We also attached a short ops note describing our traffic spikes and synthetic test details.

Best,
Lina Gomez
Head of Infrastructure | Seastone.ai
lina@seastone.ai

Attachments:
- seastone_docusign_provisioning.pdf (ops note & signature placeholder)
